> 忏者，忏其前愆……悔者，悔其后过。凡夫愚迷，只知忏其前愆，不知悔其后过。

The chapter opens with incense, and immediately removes it from the altar.

Five incenses of the self-nature's dharma-body: the incense of precepts — no wrong, no evil, no jealousy, no greed, no anger, no robbery in one's own mind. The incense of concentration — seeing good and evil states with a mind that does not become disordered. The incense of wisdom — constantly observing the self-nature with wisdom, not doing evil, doing good without clinging. The incense of liberation — the mind without dependence, not thinking good, not thinking evil, at ease. The incense of the knowledge and vision of liberation — not sinking into empty stillness, but learning widely, knowing one's own mind, *mixing light with the world, without self, without other*.

*This incense is inwardly kindled; do not seek it outside.*

Five items, each with a definition that is a description of a state. None of them requires a stick, a bowl, or a hall. The fifth is the interesting one, because it is the one that forbids its own trap: liberation is not allowed to become a retirement from contact. Not sinking into emptiness is part of the definition of liberation.

## 忏 and 悔 are not the same word

The chapter then distinguishes the two halves of a compound we use as one word:

*What is 忏? 忏 is repentance of former faults. All former evil deeds, delusion, arrogance, jealousy — fully repented, never arising again: this is 忏. What is 悔? 悔 is remorse for later faults. From now on, all evil deeds, delusion, arrogance, jealousy — now awakened to, cut off forever, never done again: this is 悔.*

The two halves map onto past and future. Then the observation that makes the whole chapter worth reading:

*Ordinary people, deluded, only know how to repent former faults and do not know remorse for later faults. Because there is no 悔, the former faults are not extinguished and later faults are born again. Former faults not extinguished, later faults reborn — what is that called repentance?*

The formula for the recitation is not a confession of items. It is three lines, each with the same shape: *former thought, present thought and next thought — thought after thought not stained by delusion* (then: by arrogance, then: by jealousy). The object of attention is the next thought, not the last deed. Repentance that only audits the past is bookkeeping; the account keeps reopening.

## The vows, rewritten in the first person

The four great vows get the same treatment. *Beings boundless, I vow to save them* becomes: the beings in my own mind — the deluded mind, the deceitful mind, the unkind mind, the jealous mind, the malicious mind. *The deluded come and I save them with awakening; the lost come and I save them with insight.*

*Each must save themselves by the self-nature — this is true salvation.* The line is careful about direction: no one else's hand does it, and the vow is not withdrawn. The scope is moved from a population to a set of states, and the work stays.

*The dharma-gates are inexhaustible, I vow to learn them* becomes 自见性，常行正法 — seeing the nature, always practicing the right dharma. *The unsurpassed buddha-way, I vow to accomplish it* becomes 常能下心 — always able to lower the mind, practice the genuine, leave delusion and awakening both, always give rise to prajna.

## 三归依 without an object

The last item: taking refuge in awakening, in rightness, in purity — *the self-nature's three treasures*, with *from today, take awakening as the teacher, no longer take refuge in deviant demons and outside ways*.

The commentary notes what this is not: it is not a rejection of the tradition he is speaking inside. He is a monk, in a robe, on a platform, citing sutras. It is a rejection of the location — refuge taken in something outside the mind is, by this chapter's logic, refuge taken in a mark.

## 一体三身

The chapter closes with the three bodies of the buddha as one body: the dharmakaya, the reward body, the transformation body, each defined by a mode of mind rather than a cosmic career. The formula is consistent with everything before it: 罪不在外，忏不在仪，佛不在他方.

## The test

Take one thing you keep apologizing for. Then separate the halves. Have you done the regret — and have you done the stopping? Most of us have done the first several times and the second zero times, and the apology has become the place where the behavior is allowed to continue.

The next thought is where 悔 lives. Not the next occasion.
